closures.item: (iv) F-D5-03(sweep) — liveEditingDrops maintenance moved to the binding half; applyEdit touches NO gesture/finger state
closures.proof: Mechanical check over the whole mutation body: `awk 'NR>=2092 && NR<=2173' AR/GeoARSessionManager.swift | grep -n 'editingDropID|heldGestures|liveEditingDrops|gestureHeld|lastLiveEditTick|beginLiveEdit|cancelLiveEdit'` returns NOTHING — applyEdit (:2092-2173) is now gesture-free; the failure arm is a bare `return` (:2102-2103) and the commit tail (:2161-2172) only clears groundLockBaseY / re-pins VPS. The two writes now live in the binding half: insert at :2059-2065 (non-commit ticks only, after the editTarget refusal gate at :2055-2057, so a stale unheld tick still inserts nothing) and release at :2075-2077 `if heldGestures == 0 { liveEditingDrops.remove(id) }`, sharing the exact predicate commitBookkeeping (:538-544) uses to clear the capture. TWO-THUMB REPLAY: heldGestures 2 → first commit → remaining 1 → capture survives (:2072-2074) and :2077's condition is false → the finger guard survives; second (last) lift → remaining 0 → capture nil AND the entry removed. AUTHORED SNAP MID-DRAG: snapNearestDropToGround (:2193-2251) calls applyEdit directly at :2248 with commit:true — it can no longer strip the entry (that removal is gone) nor decrement heldGestures, so the held thumb keeps both the VPS guard and its binding (FT-41(e) 'no dead slider'). relocateNearestDrop (:2282-2351) bypasses applyEdit entirely and never touched the set. VANISHED-DROP OWNERSHIP: placedDrops entries are destroyed at exactly two sites — resetPlacements :949 and removePerDropState :1670 — and both clear the finger state in the same block (:957-959 removeAll + capture nil + counter 0; :1678-1684 remove(id) + capture nil + counter 0). Every destroy site routes through removePerDropState (:738 clearRoomDrops, :1949 GPS reconcile, :2510 VPS/geo reconcile), which is the contract the round-6 doc comment (:2090-2091) claims. No leak path: :2058 sets editingDropID to the same id it inserts, and every capture-clearing site clears the set entry in lockstep, so the invariant `!liveEditingDrops.isEmpty ⇒ editingDropID != nil` holds; the ungated backstop at :1228-1233 therefore always reaches cancelLiveEdit (≤30 s held, ≤1.5 s unheld), and updatePowerTier's governor pin (:1258) can never outlive that bound. The one behaviour genuinely new to round 6 — insert BEFORE the resolve, so an unresolvable id can enter the set — is caught by that same bound plus the (i) terminator.

closures.item: (c) stationary finger + authored VPS snap — the case that motivated (iv)
closures.proof: Replay: thumb1 drags a little (inserts C at :2065, capture C at :2058) then holds STILL — no further ticks, and none are needed: the entry persists because nothing removes it any more. Thumb2 taps 'Place on ground' → snapNearestDropToGround resolves `nearestDrop`, which is still C because updateNearest is frozen on the capture (:1705) → applyEdit(commit:true) at :2248 leaves the set untouched. C therefore stays guarded throughout: applyVPSTransform bails at :999 and syncGPSPlacements skips at :1877-1880, so nothing fights the finger; the governor stays .full (:1258) for the duration of the hold, which is the intended pin. LAST FINGER UP: adjustNearestDrop commit → remaining 0 → :2077 removes C → :999/:1878 pass again on the next VPS/GPS pass; applyEdit's commit tail (:2166-2171) removes C from vpsOwnedDrops and calls geospatial.invalidateAnchor, so the re-resolved anchor arrives with isFirst == true and glides 1.2 s (:1012-1019) — VPS glide correctly resumes rather than snapping. The grounding disc tracks in both directions inside applyEdit (:2117 on height, :2135-2138 on scale), including on the last commit. Caveat, not a regression: a finger pressed and NEVER moved sends no ticks, so no insert ever happens and only the nearest-freeze (capture) protects that drop — identical in round 5, where the insert also lived behind the tick.

PASS: the HUD title is free to follow you again within ~1 s (it must not stay stuck on A), the sliders are live on the next press, and the phone does not run hot for the rest of the session.' reviews.reviewer: Staff Swift/ARKit reviewer — Wave D round 6 desk gate, items (i) F-D5-01 and (iv) F-D5-03 (gesture-state closures)
reviews.ship_opinion: Yes — from the gesture-state half, the field sessions may run on 701a547. Both assigned closures verify clean against the code I actually read, not against the commit messages: the panel-level .onDisappear (ARScreen.swift:301) is a genuine removal hook for all four teardown paths, is a no-op when nothing is held (GeoARSessionManager.swift:460-465 early-returns and writes no @Published state and no log line), and cannot cancel a legitimate gesture in any new way — backgrounding and the call banner never remove the cover, and those paths already cancelled through suspendSession (:441) and markCameraHidden (:640) before round 6; the app's single fullScreenCover (RootView.swift:156) means nothing is ever presented over the panel. applyEdit is now mechanically free of every gesture/finger symbol over its full body (:2092-2173), the insert/release pair sits in the binding half on the same remaining==0 predicate as the capture (:2065, :2072-2077), the authored snap at :2248 can no longer strip the guard from under a held thumb, and the deleted failure-arm remove leaves no orphan: placedDrops dies only at :949 and :1670, both of which clear the set, the capture and the counter together, so the invariant liveEditingDrops⊆{editingDropID} holds and the ungated backstop at :1228-1233 bounds any residue at 30 s — the governor can never be pinned .full for the session, which was the harm this whole thread existed to kill. I found nothing in the round-6 diff that gates the sessions, so my findings list is empty on purpose. The honest weakness is evidence, not code: neither (i) nor (iv) is covered by any unit test (the editTarget and commitBookkeeping tables are unchanged and pass either way), and (i) has no field case at all while (iv) has only FT-41(e), whose PASS wording names the round-5 symptom rather than the round-6 one. Both gaps are closable with a doc-only edit to FIELDTESTS.md that does not touch the binary; take them or leave them, but do not re-open a desk round for them.

test_vacuity.reason: Sound in itself, but untouched by round 6 and insensitive to both closures: editTarget's inputs and truth table are identical before and after. It passes unchanged on reverted (i) and reverted (iv). D3 answer for (i): NO test fails on revert, and no field case either — the only symptom is a stuck HUD title / dead sliders for up to 30 s after a mid-drag teardown plus a .full governor pin that would silently contaminate FT-28/FT-31 heat.

closures.item: (ii) F-D5-05 half 1 — no "TTFO: 0 ms" latch OR log line on a failed session (failed-session trace replayed)
closures.proof: Full replay against the current file. (1) session(_:didFailWithError:) GeoARSessionManager.swift:2860-2890 → sessionFailed = true (:2865), sessionFrameReady = false, disarmSemanticMatte; if the 5 s rate limit is open AND tickTask != nil it cold-recovers immediately (:2885 runGPSCompass), else it arms failureRetryDeadline (:2887). (2) suspendSession :423-431 cancels tickTask and CLEARS failureRetryDeadline (:430) — sessionFailed survives the suspension (only detach :393 and runGPSCompass :907 clear it). (3) return: ARSessionHolder.swift:61-70 cameraDidAppear → markCameraVisible() at :68 BEFORE startIfNeeded() at :69 (same contract at :95/:96 for appDidBecomeActive). (4) markCameraVisible :645-660: the new conjunct `!sessionFailed` at :654 is FALSE, so control takes the else arm :658 — timeToFirstObjectMs = nil, and metricsLog.log("TTFO: 0 ms (pre-warmed…)") at :656 is NOT reached. The latch AND the log line are both dead on this path; grep confirms :656 is the only emitter of the 0 ms string. (5) startIfNeeded → attached==true, sessionRunning==false → resumeSession() :565 → the sessionFailed branch :569-573 → runGPSCompass() :883 → resetPlacements() at :901, which nils timeToFirstObjectMs (:987) and restamps cameraVisibleAt (:988), so the recovery number is measured from the restart instant — consistent with the new log text at :2381. Placement of the first re-placed holder → recordTTFOIfNeeded :2375 → tagged line. No path emits a 0 ms claim over holders a reset is about to destroy. Terminal cameraUnauthorized failure (:2867-2872) also yields no latch and no log (sessionFailed stays true, nothing renders).

closures.item: (ii) F-D5-05/F-R5-10 half 2 — recovery epochs logged "TTFO (recovery)"; flag right in EVERY epoch transition (fresh appear, warm resume, failed resume, mid-session relocalize restart, attach cold start)
closures.proof: Every genuine recovery is correctly tagged, but the tag no longer DISCRIMINATES: a fresh cold start is tagged "recovery" too. Writes of ttfoEpochIsRecovery are exactly two — :648 (false, markCameraVisible) and :989 (true, resetPlacements); attach() :323-339 does NOT clear it, contrary to the closure list's "cleared by markCameraVisible/attach". Transition table: (a) FRESH APPEAR / cold start — WRONG: ARSessionHolder:68 markCameraVisible sets false, :69 startIfNeeded → :106 attach → :339 decideModeAndRun → :760 runGPSCompass (appleGeoAnchorsEnabled = false at AppConfig.swift:22, so this branch is unconditional and synchronous) → :901 resetPlacements → :989 flag = TRUE; nothing clears it before the first holder lands, so the canonical Killer-#1 number logs as "TTFO (recovery): N ms from session restart to first rendered object" (finding F-D6-TTFO-01). (b) WARM RESUME (holders survive) — CORRECT: markCameraVisible sets false and latches the honest "TTFO: 0 ms (pre-warmed)"; resumeSession :600-625 never calls resetPlacements, flag stays false. (c) FAILED RESUME — CORRECT: markCameraVisible clears to false first (ordering confirmed at ARSessionHolder:68/:95), then resumeSession :569 → runGPSCompass → resetPlacements re-sets TRUE; the ordering hint holds and the last writer wins correctly. (d) MID-SESSION RELOCALIZE RESTART :1144-1148 and DEFERRED FAILURE RETRY :1134-1138 and IMMEDIATE FAILURE RECOVERY :2885 — CORRECT: all reach resetPlacements with no markCameraVisible after (camera is already visible), so they tag recovery. (e) ATTACH COLD START via beginRevealWarmup (ARSessionHolder:55-59, no markCameraVisible) — WRONG in the same way, and worse: a holder placed during the warm-up logs "TTFO (recovery)" before the user has seen the camera, then the later markCameraVisible latches "TTFO: 0 ms (pre-warmed)". Reverse direction (a recovery epoch logging the UN-tagged line) is reachable only in one narrow shape — reset destroys content, user flips to Map and back before any re-placement, markCameraVisible clears the flag with placedHolders empty — and there the untagged reading is defensible (a genuine camera-visible→first-object measurement). The load-bearing failure is direction (a)/(e).

closures.item: (iii) F-D5-HUD — fps/p95/format line renders when ANY part exists; format only when accompanied
closures.proof: ARScreen.swift:669-677: parts is built from three independent optionals (ttfo :671, fps :672, p95 :673); `guard !parts.isEmpty else { return nil }` at :674 sits BEFORE the unconditional format append at :675, so the format string can never appear alone — exactly the stated contract. Render site :472-478 is `if let line = metricsLine()`, no TTFO gate. Verified the line survives a mid-session reset: resetPlacements :936-990 nils timeToFirstObjectMs (:987) but never touches renderFPS/frameP95Ms — grep shows their only writers are :1535 and :1561 (the rolling fps/p95 windows) and neither is ever set back to nil, so after any cold restart the line keeps rendering as "N fps · p95 M ms · <format>". videoFormatDescription is non-optional with default "?" (:139), so no empty trailing segment is constructible.

closures.item: (iii) tint — (manager.timeToFirstObjectMs ?? 0) <= 400, i.e. mint when TTFO is nil, including during a recovery epoch
closures.proof: ARScreen.swift:475-477. Acceptable, not misleading enough to gate. While TTFO is nil the rendered line contains NO "first object" segment, so the mint tint decorates a line that makes no TTFO claim; the moment the number lands the tint re-keys to it (>400 ms → yellow). Nothing in the field protocol reads the colour: FIELDTESTS.md:9 documents the HUD legend as text, FIELDTESTS.md:278 asks for the line VERBATIM ("screenshots are fine") and states the FT-28 PASS criteria numerically (fps ≥ 30, p95 ≤ 40 ms, no thermal banner). Grep for mint/yellow/green across FIELDTESTS.md returns no HUD-colour criterion. Logged as a residual (neutral tint when nil) rather than a finding.

closures.item: (iii) FT-28's "record the HUD line verbatim" works at every t including after a mid-session reset
closures.proof: Works at every t once the first fps window has closed (:1533-1537), which is seconds after camera open and long before FT-28's t=0/2/5/10 min sampling points. After a mid-session reset the line reads "N fps · p95 M ms · <format>" — the instruction is no longer blinded, which was the whole of F-D5-HUD. One doc gap, filed as a residual, not a defect: FIELDTESTS.md:278 anticipates the "first object" segment showing a RECOVERY NUMBER, but between the reset and the first re-placed holder the segment is legitimately ABSENT; an operator sampling in that window records a three-part line the note does not describe.

closures.item: (c) Sweep — anything in the two instruments' diffs the closure list did not name
closures.proof: git diff e838682..f9b9b88 over the two instruments yields exactly: markCameraVisible's flag write + !sessionFailed guard (:648/:654), resetPlacements' flag write (:989), the ttfoEpochIsRecovery declaration (:2372) and the branch in recordTTFOIfNeeded (:2380-2384); ARScreen's HUD render site (:466-478) and metricsLine signature/body (:669-677). Nothing else. The recovery line's new wording ("from session restart to first rendered object" vs "from camera visible…") is unnamed by the list but is CORRECT — resetPlacements restamps cameraVisibleAt at :988, so the reference really is the restart instant. No unnamed behavioural change, no hidden state added, no new @Published, no new call edges. (The liveEditingDrops hunks at :2056-2075/:2100-2160 and ARScreen:301 are items (iv)/(i), other seats; I read them for interaction with the instruments and found none — neither touches TTFO, epoch, or HUD state.) Also confirmed f9b9b88 is DECISIONS-only (git show --stat) and `git diff 701a547..f9b9b88 -- '*.swift'` is empty, so the code reviewed IS the field build; working tree clean.

findings.claim: The new `ttfoEpochIsRecovery = true` in resetPlacements fires on the COLD-START path too, and nothing clears it afterwards, so every fresh cold open logs the Killer-#1 number as "TTFO (recovery)". attach() (:323-339) never writes the flag — the closure list's "cleared by markCameraVisible/attach" is only half implemented — and markCameraVisible runs BEFORE attach on both entry paths (ARSessionHolder.swift:68 and :95), so its `false` at :648 is immediately overwritten by attach → decideModeAndRun (:339) → runGPSCompass (:760) → resetPlacements (:901) → :989. AppConfig.appleGeoAnchorsEnabled = false, so that chain is unconditional and synchronous: the mis-tag is deterministic on 100% of cold starts, not a race. Round 5's defect made a recovery look like a cold start; round 6 inverts it and makes every cold start look like a recovery, so the tag now discriminates nothing.
findings.harm: FT-1 and FT-2 (cold open, ×5 each — the two flagship Killer-#1 field cases) and the t=0 reading of FT-28 will each write "TTFO (recovery): N ms from session restart to first rendered object" into the logarchive for a launch where no restart occurred. FIELDTESTS.md:278 instructs the debrief that a recovery-tagged number "is NOT a Killer-#1 cold-start figure" and FIELDTESTS.md:268 says the debrief greps `TTFO`, so every genuine cold-start TTFO the four sessions produce is self-invalidated by its own label — the one Killer-#1 number the wave could harvest for free is destroyed, in the pessimistic direction this time but destroyed. Worse, it manufactures a false mid-session-restart signature at the start of every session in the exact stream S3/S4 use to judge stability (an operator cross-checking the HUD's "first object: 380 ms" against the log sees a session restart that never happened, and may report an FT-3-adjacent instability that does not exist). Same class and same stream as F-D5-05, which the counsel graded HIGH. The measured VALUE stays correct — markCameraVisible and resetPlacements restamp cameraVisibleAt sub-millisecond apart in the same main-actor runloop turn — so this is purely a labelling defect, but the label is the evidence.
findings.fix: One line in attach(), placed AFTER decideModeAndRun() at :339 (i.e. `decideModeAndRun(); ttfoEpochIsRecovery = false  // an attach's own cold run IS the cold start`). Placement matters and is the trap: clearing at attach ENTRY next to `timeToFirstObjectMs = nil` (:328) — the naive reading of "cleared by markCameraVisible/attach" — does NOT work, because runGPSCompass → resetPlacements re-sets it to true inside the same call. The clear must land after decideModeAndRun returns. This leaves every real recovery path untouched: the deferred retry (:1138), the relocalize-stall restart (:1148), the immediate failure recovery (:2885) and the failed-resume branch (:570) all call runGPSCompass OUTSIDE attach and keep their true flag. (The flag-gated-off async runGeoTracking upgrade at :763-772 would still tag its restart as recovery, which is correct — it genuinely destroys placements.) Then re-tag the field build and re-pin the round-6 evidence line. If the owner refuses another build, the minimum acceptable substitute is a written debrief rule in FIELDTESTS.md that the FIRST "TTFO (recovery)" line after each app launch IS the cold-start figure — but the one-liner is smaller and restores the instrument's meaning instead of papering over it.

closures.item: (ii)/(ix) ride-along — TTFO recovery-epoch tagging and the S3 debrief note that reads it
closures.proof: The new epoch flag is set true inside resetPlacements (GeoARSessionManager.swift:989), which the COLD path also runs (runGPSCompass :901, reached from attach :339 via decideModeAndRun :760). ARSessionHolder.cameraDidAppear calls markCameraVisible (clearing the flag, :648) BEFORE startIfNeeded (ARSessionHolder.swift:68-69), so on every ordinary cold open the flag ends TRUE and the Killer-#1 first-object line is emitted as 'TTFO (recovery)' (:2380-2381). FIELDTESTS.md:278 instructs the debrief that such a number 'is NOT a Killer-#1 cold-start figure'. See F-D6-01.

findings.claim: The round-6 recovery-epoch flag is set in resetPlacements(), which the COLD start also runs, so on every ordinary cold open the Killer-#1 TTFO is emitted as 'TTFO (recovery)'. Trace: ARSessionHolder.cameraDidAppear (ARSessionHolder.swift:68-69) calls markCameraVisible() first — which sets ttfoEpochIsRecovery = false (:648) and, with placedHolders empty, nils timeToFirstObjectMs — and only then startIfNeeded() -> attach() (:339) -> decideModeAndRun() (:760) -> runGPSCompass() -> resetPlacements() (:901), whose last statement sets ttfoEpochIsRecovery = true (:989). Nothing clears it again before the first object renders (markCameraVisible has only two callers, ARSessionHolder.swift:68 and :95, both of which run before attach on this path), so recordTTFOIfNeeded takes the recovery branch (:2380) and logs 'TTFO (recovery): X ms from session restart to first rendered object'. The inverse case is also wrong-signed: the deep-link path (beginRevealWarmup -> attach, then cameraDidAppear -> markCameraVisible) ends with the flag FALSE and is labelled as a cold start. Before round 6 every line read 'TTFO:' and the label carried no claim; the round-6 diff introduced the mislabel.
findings.harm: FIELDTESTS.md:278 tells the S3 debrief that a 'TTFO (recovery)' number 'is NOT a Killer-#1 cold-start figure'. On 701a547 every cold-open TTFO in the field sessions — FT-1, FT-2, and the t=0 reading of FT-28 — carries that tag, so the supervisor either discards the only Killer-#1 evidence the sessions produce or, worse, accepts a bad cold-start number as a benign 'recovery'. This is the same evidence-integrity class as F-D5-05 (a false line in the exact metrics stream the debrief reads, in the direction a field run cannot detect), reintroduced by F-D5-05's own fix.
findings.fix: The epoch's provenance is known at the call site, not at the reset. Leave resetPlacements setting the flag true (it is the correct default for every mid-session restart) and add one line to attach(), after decideModeAndRun() at :339: `ttfoEpochIsRecovery = false` — attach IS the cold epoch by definition (it already nils timeToFirstObjectMs on entry at :328 for exactly that reason) and it runs exactly once per launch (manager.detach() has no caller in the app). Equivalent alternative: stop setting it in resetPlacements and set it true only in the two recovery entries (resumeSession's sessionFailed branch :569-573 and any mid-session runGPSCompass). Either way re-verify with one launch and one deliberate failure recovery that the first line reads 'TTFO:' and the second reads 'TTFO (recovery):'.

findings.claim: FT-41 step 4 ('Walk two or three steps toward B — far enough that B would normally become the nearest drop') is the step that must force the nearest flip, but nothing in the case verifies it happened, and the discrimination is one-sided. With the fix WORKING the title never flips because updateNearest returns at its guard (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1705) regardless of how far the tester walked; with the fix BROKEN the flip only happens if the app's own nearest computation actually crosses. For two GEO drops that computation is `$0.location.distance(from: location)` against the raw CoreLocation fix (:1726-1730) over a 3–5 m baseline — a separation well inside typical horizontal accuracy, and both endpoints are themselves GPS-derived. So 'two or three steps' (~1.5–2.3 m) may not move the app's nearest at all, and a broken build produces the same observation as a fixed one: no flip, reported ✓(c).
findings.harm: FT-41 is, by its own first line and by FIELDTESTS.md:283, the ONLY guard on the round-5 blocker fix and a failure re-opens the wave. As written it can be reported ✓ having exercised nothing, so the wave closes on a guard that proved nothing — the exact vacuity class rounds 4 and 5 spent two rounds removing from the unit suite.
findings.fix: Add a control that measures what the APP believes, not what the tester walked. Two sentences: (1) before starting, dry-run it with no fingers down — walk the same two or three steps and confirm the HUD title flips A -> B, then walk back; if it does not flip, move the drops further apart or start closer to A. (2) After step 5's release, the title MUST flip to B within about a second (the capture clears at the last finger, GeoARSessionManager.swift:538-544, and updateNearest unfreezes on the next 400 ms tick); if it does not, the walk never crossed the boundary — the run is INCOMPLETE, not a pass, and must be repeated.

findings.claim: Variant (e) exercises the right PATH but asserts the wrong THING, so it would pass identically on the round-5 code it is meant to guard. Its pass criteria are 'the held slider still edits A afterwards (no dead slider, no jump to another drop)' and 'the tap's snap took effect' — both are properties of the CAPTURE, which round 5 already fixed: snapNearestDropToGround calls applyEdit directly with an explicit target (GeoARSessionManager.swift:2248), never touching heldGestures or editingDropID, so under round-5 code the capture survives the tap and the held slider keeps editing A. What round 6 actually changed is the FINGER GUARD: round-5 applyEdit removed the drop from liveEditingDrops on any commit, including this authored one, and round 6 moved that maintenance to the binding half (:2065 insert on tick, :2077 remove only at heldGestures == 0). Nothing in variant (e) observes liveEditingDrops' effects — the VPS never-fight-the-finger guard (:999), the deferred-correction skips (:1068, :1091), the GPS re-sync skip (:1878), the perceptual-rescale skip (:2742) and the governor's live-edit pin (:1258).
findings.harm: Variant (e) is recorded as the guard for F-D5-03, and F-D5-03 has no unit coverage (no test constructs the manager). As written a green FT-41(e) is evidence for the round-5 behaviour only; a regression that re-introduced the authored-commit strip would still report ✓, and the symptom it would produce in the field — the drop gliding or re-snapping under a stationary thumb, and the tier chip leaving FULL mid-drag — is precisely what the case does not ask anyone to look at.
findings.fix: Add the observable to (e): 'After the tap, KEEP the height thumb down and hold it still for about five seconds without releasing. The drop must not move, glide, or re-snap on its own during that hold, and the tier chip must stay FULL — any self-motion under a held finger is a FAIL, ✗(e). Then continue dragging and release.' That is the only window in which the round-5 strip was observable (the next non-commit tick re-inserts at :2065), and a stationary hold is exactly what makes it observable.

findings.claim: The round-6 dwell-floor note narrows the SCOPE of the assertion correctly but leaves the assertion itself mis-stated against the code. The code imposes a floor on one direction only: a detach requires passShouldDetach(idleFor > 5, attachedFor > 10) (GeoARSessionManager.swift:550-554, applied at :1377-1381), so every ATTACH -> DETACH interval is >= 10 s; but an attach is immediate the moment passNeeded is true (:1365-1374) with no floor at all, so a DETACH -> ATTACH interval of one 400 ms tick is designed behaviour. 'No two toggles within 10 s' therefore condemns a legal, by-construction pair — e.g. person leaves frame, hysteresis expires, 5 s idle, detach at attached=12 s, person re-enters 2 s later, immediate re-attach.
findings.harm: S4's PASS condition (FIELDTESTS.md:280) is scored on this assertion against the logarchive's attach/detach timeline. A supervisor applying it literally will read normal tier churn as a dwell-floor violation and re-open the wave on designed behaviour — a false FAIL on the leg-4 soak, which is the one leg that exists to stress this surface.
findings.fix: Restate the assertion in the direction the code actually guarantees: 'Every ATTACH -> DETACH interval must be >= 10 s and must follow >= 5 s with no work; a DETACH -> ATTACH interval has NO floor by design (work returns, the pass re-attaches on the next tick) and must not be counted. Interruption detaches (call banner, Control Center, app switch, tab-flip past grace, session failure) bypass the floor by design — GeoARSessionManager.swift:396, :432, :2840, :2866 — and are excluded.'

findings.claim: The new incomplete-decline rule contradicts two surviving sentences in its own case. (1) FIELDTESTS.md:238 still labels a decline 'a designed PASS-decline' — the token whose ambiguity the round-6 rule exists to remove — three lines above the sentence saying a decline-only run is not a pass. (2) The new retry instruction 'indoors on a hard floor is acceptable' collides with the case preamble at :235, which mandates a self-created GEO drop placed outdoors and explicitly excludes both the demo drop and room drops because only the geo drop exercises the persist assertion (d); a geo drop cannot be created or approached indoors without a GPS fix (the app's own honesty rule, FT-23), so the indoor retry pushes the tester toward exactly the drop type the case forbids.
findings.harm: FT-40 is one of the three cases that can re-open the wave (:283) and its report token feeds the closing ADR. A tester who reads the bullets before the paragraph reports '✓-decline' on a decline-only run (the loophole, still open in the reader's mind), or completes the retry on a room drop and reports ✓ for a case in which assertion (d) proved nothing about `library.update(persist: true)`.
findings.fix: Two edits: change ':238' to read 'that is a designed decline, not a pass — the case is not complete until a snap has been evaluated'; and change the retry surface to one that keeps the drop a geo drop — 'repeat on a paved area, garage floor, or doorway where GPS still fixes; the drop must still be the geo drop you created (a room drop does not exercise assertion (d))'.

findings.claim: S3 step 3 asks for 'FT-3 tab flip ×5' and then makes the debrief conditional on a '>10 s return', but no step guarantees one exists in the log. FT-3's own text (FIELDTESTS.md:25-27) prescribes a return 'within 5 s'; a sub-5 s flip never suspends at all (ARSessionHolder.schedulePause :115-125 fires only after AppConfig.pauseGraceSeconds = 5, and startIfNeeded :109 only resumes when sessionRunning is false), so no resume happens and the double-run surface is never entered. Even a tester who also does FT-3's '>5 s away' leg may return at 7 s, which does not match the debrief's '>10 s' criterion.
findings.harm: The regression check for F-D3-02 — one of the two round-3 blockers, with no unit coverage — can report clean by having produced no qualifying event. It is the same silent-nothing-to-see failure mode as F-D6-02, on the third of the three wave-gating cases.
findings.fix: Make the precondition an instruction: 'FT-3 ×5 — at least TWO of the five returns must be after 15+ s away (past the 5 s pause grace, so the session really suspends and warm-resumes); note the wall-clock time of those two returns so the debrief can look at the right place in the log.'

findings.claim: The round-6 leg-3 restatement is right about the hierarchy but overstates by one word: 'the only locks acquired while it is held are the leaf feed locks'. The round-5 version carried the qualifier 'in-app'; without it the sentence is literally false, and its own parenthetical enumerates the callouts incompletely — it names CoreVideo/Metal (the flush and the CPU-side encode) but not os_log, which encode() also performs under the lock via logDepthBoundsIfChanged (SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:376 -> :496-500), and os_log takes framework-internal locks and writes to the shared log store. The companion clause 'which take no callouts' is likewise approximate: SemanticFeed.snapshot()/clear() retain and release CVPixelBuffers inside the lock body (:34-38, :44-50).
findings.harm: This is the sentence a future maintainer is told was 're-verified each counsel closure round', written specifically because the round-5 wording 'would have misdirected a maintainer into re-introducing the RENDER-4 stall'. Read literally it licenses adding more logging or CF work under stateLock on the render thread — the exact latency the record elsewhere says the main actor must not queue behind. The inversion-freedom conclusion itself is sound and I confirmed it; only the enumeration overstates.
findings.fix: Restore the qualifier and complete the list: 'the only IN-APP locks acquired while it is held are the leaf feed locks (SemanticFeed.lock, MidFieldDepthFeed.lock), whose bodies take no other lock and never call back into the pass, so no in-app lock-order inversion is constructible (stateLock IS held across framework callouts by design — the CVMetalTextureCache flush, the CPU-side encode, and one rate-limited os_log at :376; no further work belongs under it).'

test_vacuity.test: FT-41 steps 1–5, assertion (c) 'the HUD title stayed A for the entire interaction'
test_vacuity.reason: It WOULD fail on the round-4 code — but only conditionally. Under round-4's applyEdit the height release cleared the shared capture, updateNearest (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1705) unfroze, and the guidance card's drop.title (ARScreen.swift:709) would flip to B within one 400 ms tick, and the panel's .onChange(of: nearestDrop?.id) (ARScreen.swift:619) would also visibly jump the slider thumbs. The condition is that the app's own nearest actually crosses, which is computed from raw GPS over a 3–5 m baseline (:1726-1730) — and no step in the case verifies that it did. As written a tester who under-walks observes 'no flip' on broken code and reports ✓. Non-vacuous only after F-D6-02's control step is added.

Named assertions are 'the held slider still edits A afterwards' and 'the tap's snap took effect'. Both hold on the round-5 code: snapNearestDropToGround routes to applyEdit with an explicit target (GeoARSessionManager.swift:2248) and never touched heldGestures or editingDropID even before round 6, so the capture survived and the slider kept editing A. The round-6 change is liveEditingDrops maintenance (:2065, :2077, and the deletions at old :2103/:2113/:2162), whose effects — VPS glide (:999), deferred corrections (:1068/:1091), GPS re-sync (:1878), perceptual rescale (:2742), governor pin (:1258) — variant (e) never asks anyone to observe. It cannot distinguish 701a547 from abe4f50.

It changes the recorded outcome of a real, reachable run: a session where snapNearestDropToGround takes its honest decline branch (GeoARSessionManager.swift:2231-2239, showPersistError non-critical) every time was reportable as '✓-decline' under the round-5 wording and is now 'incomplete (declined ×N)'. The named assertion is the report token itself, and the loophole it closes is the one the round-5 counsel identified.

test_vacuity.test: S3 step 3's FT-3 debrief check: no 'Perception recon=' within ~1 s of a >10 s return
test_vacuity.reason: The check itself is mechanically sound — it would have caught F-D3-02, because under the round-3 code the resume plan's visibility conjunct was invariantly false, so the first tick raised reconstruction and setPerception (GeoARSessionManager.swift:920-933) emitted the line within 400 ms; under the round-4/5/6 code resumeSession assigns appliedPerception directly (:613) from the same shared predicate the tick uses, so no line is emitted. But nothing in the procedure guarantees a >10 s return exists in the log (FT-3 prescribes <5 s, which never even suspends), so the check can report clean on zero qualifying events. Non-vacuous once F-D6-06's instruction is added.

Not vacuous — it is wrong-signed. It will fire on legal timelines: passShouldDetach floors only the attach->detach interval (GeoARSessionManager.swift:550-554), while re-attach on returning work is immediate (:1365-1374), so a detach->attach pair 400 ms apart is designed behaviour and would be scored as a violation. It fails on correct code, which is the opposite failure to vacuity and equally disqualifying for a pass/fail bar.

The named assertion is XCTAssertNotNil(view.renderCallbacks.postProcess) after setCallbacksActive(true). It fails against any regression that re-weakens the hold on the view: the pass stores it in a weak var (SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:76) and setCallbacksActive bails at 'guard changed, let arView' (:195), so restoring the round-5 form — prepare(on: ARView(frame:.zero)) with no strong local — releases the temporary before the first toggle and this assertion goes nil. The paired XCTAssertNil after detach also pins the clearing half (:212-213). This is a genuine guard, not a tautology, and it is the reason the round-6 leg-1 evidence line can claim the slot assignments executed.

reviews.ship_opinion: Not cleanly on 701a547 as it stands, though nothing I found threatens the device, the user, or the app's behaviour — every defect in my scope threatens the EVIDENCE the four sessions exist to produce, which is the same standard the supervisor used to justify calling round 6 in the first place. Items (vi)–(ix) all landed and the record is materially more honest than round 5's: leg-1's power is now stated at its true scope and I verified it against the probe, leg-3's two-level hierarchy is correct at mechanism level (encode holds stateLock across both leaf feed snapshots, and neither leaf lock can call back), leg 5's floor-not-census framing and pinned command are accurate and the setting really is on this SHA, the MetricKit caveats match the code, and the round-5 corrections check out line by line. But the round-6 diff introduced one defect that inverts the very instrument the protocol reads: because the recovery-epoch flag is set inside resetPlacements, which the cold path also runs, every cold-open TTFO on 701a547 is emitted as 'TTFO (recovery)' — the exact line FIELDTESTS.md:278 tells the debrief to discard as not-Killer-#1 — while the deep-link path is labelled the other way round. That is one line to fix (set the flag false at the end of attach()) and it costs a new SHA plus a desk re-run, which is cheap against mis-reading Killer #1 in all four sessions. The three protocol items are docs-only and do not move the binary: FT-41 needs its boundary-crossing control or it can be reported ✓ having exercised nothing, variant (e) needs an assertion that actually watches the finger guard or it is a round-5 test wearing a round-6 label, and S4's dwell-floor sentence needs re-signing or it will fail the soak on designed behaviour. My recommendation: land the one-line TTFO fix and the ~8 lines of FIELDTESTS/DECISIONS wording, re-run the desk gate on the new SHA, and go. If the owner would rather not move off 701a547, the sessions can still run provided the debrief is told in writing that on this build the first TTFO line after every launch is mislabelled '(recovery)', and provided the FIELDTESTS amendments land first — they are not compiled into the app and so do not invalidate 701a547 as the binary under test.

research.researcher: Industry researcher (5th counsel seat) — Wave D round 6, FINAL desk ruling on build 701a547 (docs tail f9b9b88)

validations.claim: TEST_RUNNER_TSAN_OPTIONS is the correct xcodebuild mechanism for delivering env vars to test-runner processes, and the round-5 SIMCTL_CHILD_ prefix was not.
validations.basis: Primary source, run locally: `man xcodebuild` ENVIRONMENT section — "TEST_RUNNER_<VAR>: Set an environment variable whose name is prefixed with TEST_RUNNER_ to have that variable passed, with its prefix stripped, to all test runner processes launched during a test action." Counterpart primary source `xcrun simctl spawn` help — "If you want to set environment variables in the resulting environment, set them in the calling environment with a SIMCTL_CHILD_ prefix", i.e. scoped to processes simctl itself spawns, not to a runner launched by xcodebuild/testmanagerd. The round-6 wording in DECISIONS.md:1202 and :1206 is exactly right.

validations.claim: No iOS-device TSan runtime ships in any Xcode (clang toolchain carries tsan_iossim/tsan_osx/tsan_xros, no tsan_ios).
validations.basis: Verified on this machine, Xcode 26.6 (17F113), clang 21.0.0: /Applications/Xcode.app/.../clang/21.0.0/lib/darwin contains libclang_rt.tsan_iossim_dynamic.dylib, tsan_osx, tsan_tvossim, tsan_watchossim, tsan_xros, tsan_xrossim — and no tsan_ios. Two nits for the record, neither load-bearing: the enumeration omits the tvossim/watchossim/xrossim variants, and "in any Xcode" is a universal claim evidenced here only for 26.6 — suggest "in any shipping Xcode to date (verified 26.6 / clang 21)".

validations.claim: Leg-3 restatement: stateLock is the OUTER lock of a strict two-level hierarchy; only leaf feed locks are taken under it, never the reverse.
validations.basis: SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:68-69 header — "Lock ordering invariant: `stateLock` may be held while acquiring a feed lock (SemanticFeed/MidFieldDepthFeed), NEVER the reverse" — and :80-82 on the declaration; SemanticFeed's own lock is a leaf NSLock (:13-45, no callouts). The round-6 sentence in DECISIONS.md:1202 matches the file's own documented invariant; the round-5 wording it replaced was indeed false against encode()'s feed snapshots.

validations.claim: Round-6 evidence paragraph (DECISIONS.md:1206) is an accurate record of the described runs.
validations.basis: The leg-1 half is accurate and correctly pinned to 701a547. The leg-5 half is not: the paragraph states device 149/149 TWICE and 114 TWICE, and the sentence "Device suite on the same SHA: 149/149. Leg 5 executed on the same SHA: SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY = complete is now SET … build green: 114 unique concurrency diagnostics" plus the whole per-type triage is round-5 (abe4f50) material moved verbatim out of :1204 and re-attributed to 701a547 — the build-setting change landed in abe4f50, and only the TOTAL (114) was recounted on 701a547. Symmetrically, :1204 still carries the title "Leg-1 and leg-5 evidence, round 5" but now contains no leg-5 evidence and no device count at all. See finding F-RSCH6-02.

validations.claim: Round-6 leg-1 run had halt_on_error=1 in effect.
validations.basis: The delivery MECHANISM is documented (man xcodebuild, above), but a run with zero ThreadSanitizer: reports never exercises halt_on_error, so the run itself yields no positive evidence that TSAN_OPTIONS arrived in the runner. The record's phrasing "(the corrected, test-runner-reaching prefix)" is a mechanism claim, not an observed one — fine if stated that way (F-RSCH6-03). grep -c 'ThreadSanitizer:' == 0 stands on its own either way, exactly as the amendment already says.

validations.claim: The probe's new coverage assertions are a durable guard against leg-1 vacuity.
validations.basis: Durable against the round-5 vacuity class only. WaveDTests.swift:585-594 runs prepare/setCallbacksActive/assert on the MAIN thread before the concurrent phase, and :618 withExtendedLifetime keeps the weak view alive through the 4000-toggle join — so a deallocated view or rotted prepare(on:) now fails loudly. It does NOT pin WHO writes the slots: if setCallbacksActive is annotated @MainActor — the change the same record names as a Wave E candidate (DECISIONS.md:1206) — or gains an internal hop to main, the concurrent half goes silently single-threaded while all four assertions still pass and the only other assertions (:622-623, reads > 0 and observedActive >= 0) are tautologies. That is the silent-vacuity path that remains open (F-RSCH6-04).

validations.claim: Settings → Developer → Hang Detection exists on current iOS and 250 ms is a valid threshold for the S3/S4 instruction.
validations.basis: Apple WWDC22 session 10082 "Track down hangs with Xcode and on-device detection" plus current secondary confirmations: on-device hang detection lives in Settings → Developer → Hang Detection (iOS 16+, requires Developer Mode; works for development-signed and TestFlight apps — precisely this build's case). Nuance worth writing into FIELDTESTS: 250 ms is the SHORTEST selectable on-device threshold (raisable to 500 ms+), not an arbitrary pick — Instruments is the only route below it. So the protocol's "threshold 250 ms" is the floor and is correct as written. Sources: https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2022/10082/ , https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/763010

validations.claim: MetricKit delivery caveat: inert in Xcode-installed builds, and reports events with no session denominator.
validations.basis: Consistent across Apple guidance and field reports: real MXMetricPayload/MXDiagnosticPayload delivery is limited to App Store/TestFlight installs (Xcode's Debug → Simulate MetricKit Payload is the dev-build substitute), and payloads arrive at most daily, beginning ~24 h after first launch. Even under the most generous reading of dev-build delivery, the daily cadence alone makes it inert inside a same-day four-session field day — I recommend the record carry that second, unarguable reason alongside the first. The no-denominator point is inherent to the API (event payloads, no session count). Sources: https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2020/10081/ , https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/766016

validations.claim: The S3/S4 log-capture and grep instructions actually resolve against this build.

own_findings.claim: The round-6 TTFO recovery tag is INVERTED on the cold-start path: every genuine cold start is logged "TTFO (recovery)". Trace: ARSessionHolder.cameraDidAppear (ARSessionHolder.swift:61-70) calls markCameraVisible() FIRST, which sets ttfoEpochIsRecovery = false (GeoARSessionManager.swift:648), and only then startIfNeeded() (ARSessionHolder.swift:100-113) → attach() (:323) → decideModeAndRun() (:748-761) → runGPSCompass() (:883) → resetPlacements() (:901) → ttfoEpochIsRecovery = true (:989). Nothing clears it again before the first object renders, so recordTTFOIfNeeded (:2374-2386) takes the :2380 branch and emits "TTFO (recovery): N ms from session restart to first rendered object" for the app's ordinary cold start. The flag's real semantics on 701a547 are "this epoch began at resetPlacements", which includes the first attach.
own_findings.harm: FT-28/S3 step 4 is the wave's only Killer-#1 (median ≤ 400 ms) field evidence, and FIELDTESTS.md's S3 note instructs the debrief that a line reading "TTFO (recovery)" is NOT a cold-start figure. Followed literally against this build, every cold-start number in all four sessions is discarded and no epoch is left labelled cold — the discrimination round 6 was added to buy is not merely absent but reversed. The magnitude of the number is unaffected (both branches log the same ms), so this is an evidence-labelling defect, not a metric defect.
own_findings.fix: Preferred, NO rebuild (keeps the field build pinned at 701a547): one docs-only commit on top of f9b9b88 stating the tag's true semantics — "on 701a547 the (recovery) tag marks any epoch that began at resetPlacements, which INCLUDES the first cold attach; the cold-start number is the FIRST TTFO line after each process launch in the archive; a true mid-session recovery epoch is one preceded in the same process by 'Deferred session-failure recovery firing' (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1137), 'Relocalization stalled — falling back to cold restart' (:1147), or a failed-session tab-return" — amended into the S3 step-4 note in FIELDTESTS.md and the round-6 line in DECISIONS.md:1206. Code fix belongs in the FIRST post-field commit, not now: clear the flag at the end of attach() (after decideModeAndRun(), GeoARSessionManager.swift:339) — a fresh attach is by definition a cold start. Taking the code fix now changes the SHA and forces a full desk re-run (device 149/149 + TSan leg + leg-5 recount) for a log tag whose number is already correct.

own_findings.claim: The round-6 evidence paragraph duplicates and re-attributes round-5 measurements. DECISIONS.md:1206 states "Device suite on the same SHA: 149/149" a second time and "114" a second time, and the clause "Leg 5 executed on the same SHA: SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY = complete is now SET on the app target's build configurations … build green: 114 unique concurrency diagnostics" together with the entire per-type triage (SemanticOcclusionPass 6, PersonSentinel 2, DropStore 16, DropEntityFactory 55, …) is verbatim abe4f50 material lifted out of :1204 and now attributed to 701a547 — the build-setting change landed in round 5, and only the TOTAL was recounted on the field SHA. Symmetrically, :1204 still reads "Leg-1 and leg-5 evidence, round 5" while containing no leg-5 evidence and no device count.
own_findings.harm: Same species of defect the round-6 corrections exist to eliminate: a measurement performed on one SHA recorded as performed on another, in a record whose whole authority rests on the RSCH4-07 pinning rule. Anyone re-deriving the leg-5 triage on 701a547 and getting a different per-type split would find the record indefensible, and the round-5 line no longer supports its own title.
own_findings.fix: Docs-only, same commit as F-RSCH6-01: in :1206 delete the duplicated "Device suite on the same SHA: 149/149. Leg 5 executed on the same SHA: … build green: 114 unique concurrency diagnostics." sentence and re-head the triage as "Triage of the counsel-named subset (measured on abe4f50; total unchanged at 114 on 701a547, no per-type re-triage run)"; restore to :1204 the two facts that belong to abe4f50 — device suite 149/149, and leg 5 executed there with SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY = complete set on the app target, 114 diagnostics.

own_findings.claim: The probe's coverage assertions (WaveDTests.swift:585-594) execute only in the main-thread prologue; the concurrent half (4000 toggles at :598-604, joined at :618) has no assertion that the slot writes happened OFF the main thread or happened at all during that phase — its two assertions (:622-623) are tautological by design.
own_findings.harm: The Wave E change the record itself names — annotating setCallbacksActive @MainActor — would make the toggler hop to the main actor and silently drain leg 1 of its only cross-thread slot exercise, with all four new assertions still green. The vacuity class round 6 closed would return through a different door.
own_findings.fix: Wave E, non-blocking: inside the toggler closure record `Thread.isMainThread` into a flag and XCTAssertFalse it after the join, and count observed installs from the toggler queue (e.g. increment when view.renderCallbacks.postProcess != nil) asserting > 0 after the join. Both fail loudly the moment the writes migrate to the main actor or stop happening.
